Subject: OneTrust profile - evidence export & ask

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We finished an export of our OneTrust profile and the CAIQ fragments for the services we use; the attached zip contains the export + raw evidence. Two asks from our side:

- Can Redwood help split the OneTrust profile into a minimal public-facing bundle and a private evidence bundle (the latter kept in our S3 bucket with presigned links)?
- We also want to compact large CAIQ fragments (there's a lot of duplicated syslog/sample artifacts) so that the portal upload size stays under the 100MB window for automated ingest.

Drew and I are flexible on timing — if you want a 30-min screen share to review the export, happy to set one later this week.

Attachments: brightleaf-evidence-export.zip (manifest + raw PDFs)

Thanks,

Subject: Re: OneTrust profile - evidence export & ask

Hi Alex — thanks for the export, I downloaded the zip and skimmed the manifest. We can do the split and the CAIQ compaction; propose the following approach so we can scope work and avoid re-uploads: 

1) We will produce a minimal public bundle (policy statements, high-level CAIQ answers, non-sensitive diagrams) that you can host in OneTrust as the profile.
2) A private evidence bundle (raw PDFs, logs, KMS proofs) will remain in Brightleaf S3; we will store references (presigned URLs) in OneTrust fields reserved for evidence links.
3) For CAIQ fragments: Markus will run a compaction script that deduplicates identical attachments and replaces inline samples with hash references; the process will generate an attachments manifest (CSV) and a reduced JSON CAIQ that preserves answer fidelity.

Can you grant us read access to the S3 path or send short-lived presigned URLs so Markus can perform the compact step? If you prefer, we can run the compaction in a Redwoods sandbox and return a new zip.

Proposed timeline: initial compaction run + mapping draft by Wed (7/7), review with your team Thurs (7/8). If that works I’ll kick off the internal ticket.

Attaching an initial checklist and proposed roles.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust profile - evidence export & ask

Hi all,

I pulled a quick sample from the manifest inside brightleaf-evidence-export.zip. Notes from a technical perspective: 

- The largest files are repeated TLS cert bundles and verbose syslog exports from two hosts. We can dedupe these by content-hash and replace in CAIQ payloads with content-hash references — this reduces portal size without changing answers.
- For automation, I wrote a small shell helper (caiaq-compact.sh) that:
  * indexes attachments by SHA256,
  * extracts minimal narrative into a reduced CAIQ JSON,
  * emits profile-mapping.csv (field -> evidence-hash mapping).
- Security note: If we run the script in Redwood's sandbox, we will only store hashes and the reduced CAIQ; raw artifacts remain in your S3 unless you opt to ship them to our sandbox.

Request: please provide either: 
A) Presigned S3 read URLs for the bucket subpath (valid 72 hours) so I can run the compaction against your objects, or
B) If you prefer not to share, re-upload a representative subset (one of each artifact type) and I’ll demonstrate the compaction locally.

Estimated effort: two engineer-days for compaction + mapping generation; 0.5 day to update OneTrust profile fields and test upload.

I attached the compaction script as a stub — feel free to review before we execute.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Infrastructure Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

- After acceptance, Redwood will push the minimal public bundle into OneTrust and store the private references in the OneTrust evidence fields (no raw file upload into our tenant).
